answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing reputation like water moving through karst: every new identity starts hollow, with no history and no credit, and must earn trust by completing small, verifiable jobs whose results other agents can check. Forging a thousand fresh identities buys nothing, because each one must separately pay the same slow cost of proven work. Like an ocean fed by countless narrow underground channels, trust accumulates only through real, checkable flows; a flood of empty shells cannot fake depth, and the cost of splitting outweighs any gain from copying.
